narrative.overview: Stacked treats lunch like a modular building system. Every ingredient is a brick, every screen is assembled from bricks that stack, snap, and settle, and building your own sandwich is the same tactile joy as clicking parts together. The feeling is a well-made designer construction set — precise, colorful, satisfying to handle — not a children's toy. The energy comes from color and motion, not clutter: one hero color (Punch) owns large fields and the primary action, depth is literal with a soft two-layer stack shadow, and type is built rather than decorative. It deliberately rejects the category defaults: warm-cream-plus-serif artisanal food, kindergarten primary-only toy palettes, chalkboard-deli clichés, and neobrutalist hard shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Modular grid; everything snaps to an 8px brick unit.
Chunky rounded brick forms with one consistent corner family.
One hero color at page scale; the rest of the palette is earned, not sprinkled.
Dark ink on bright bricks — the confident, accessible, modern reading.
Real soft-stack depth with a springy press-settle as the single signature motion.
Installable PWA, themed to the brand down to the browser chrome.

rules.name: The One-Loud-Brick Rule
rules.body: Punch owns the big fields and the single primary action on a screen. The rest of the palette appears only as ingredient bricks, selections, and states — a few at a time, never a page-wide rainbow.

rules.name: The Dark-Ink-On-Bright Rule
rules.body: Every bright brick (Punch, Berry, Zest, Sky, Sun) takes Char ink, not white. It passes contrast and reads more confident and modern. Grape is the sole exception that carries white.

rules.name: The Constructed-Headline Rule
rules.body: Bricolage carries every heading; Hanken carries everything read in running text. Never swap them, never add a third display face, never letterspace Bricolage open.

rules.name: The Stack-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Bricks always rest on the two-layer stack shadow, and pressing settles them (translateY(3px) + pressed shadow). No flat zero-blur block shadows, no zero-offset colored halos.

dos: Do let Punch own whole fields and the single primary action; keep other colors meaning-bearing.
Do put dark Char ink on every bright brick (Grape is the only white-text exception).
Do give bricks the two-layer stack shadow and the translateY(3px) snap-settle on press.
Do snap every element to the 8px brick unit and the 1200px content grid.
Do author real, appetizing sandwich imagery and label synthetic content.
Do theme the PWA and browser surfaces to the palette.
donts: Don't fall back to warm-cream grounds, serif display, or chalkboard-deli cliches.
Don't use a primary-only kindergarten palette or literal LEGO trademarks.
Don't use hard zero-blur block shadows or zero-offset colored halos for depth.
Don't use gradient text, glass/blur decoration, or empty soft-shadowed rounded rectangles as content.
Don't add an eyebrow/kicker label above headings, or letterspace Bricolage open.
Don't scatter the snap motion across every hover — it is one authored moment per interaction.
